This enzyme is identified as a target of two different compounds: [(3R,4S,5S,6R)-4-acetyloxy-6-[(2S,5R,6R)-5-acetyloxy-6-[(8S,9S,10R,13S,14S,17S)-10,13-dimethyl-3-oxo-1,2,6,7,8,9,11,12,14,15,16,17-dodecahydrocyclopenta[a]phenanthren-17-yl]-6-hydroxy-2-methylheptoxy]-5-hydroxyoxan-3-yl] acetate and Methyl threo-9,10-Dihydroxyoctadecanoate. Both of these compounds are predicted to interact with DNA polymerase iota, which in turn is predicted to target COLO-829. The scores for these interactions are consistent, indicating a plausible biological pathway. The evidence suggests that 8-Oxopalmatine may act as a modulator of DNA polymerase iota, potentially influencing the activity of COLO-829 through this enzyme. The mechanism is supported by the shared target relationship between 8-Oxopalmatine and DNA polymerase iota, and the downstream effect on COLO-829. The strength of the evidence is consistent across the two paths, but further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the direct interaction between 8-Oxopalmatine and COLO-829.
